title: peak_cost (the published projected capacity charge) sums the k SMALLEST window excesses
claim: tariff._exact_topk_sum returns sum(np.sort(excess)[:k]), the k smallest, so with peak_distinct_days off the published OptimizationResult.peak_cost on the capacity_tariff plan is 0.0-3.34 against 23.2-41.5 for the k largest on all 8 price shapes; the solver's scalar surrogate takes the same arm when at most k windows tie, while its batch twin takes the largest.
mechanism: tariff.py:918. _peak_charge feeds it for peak_cost; _plateau_aware_topk_sum uses it for k>1 off plateaus, while _plateau_aware_topk_sum_batch uses np.sort(...)[:, -k:] (largest): the objective and its batched twin disagree. Inert under distinct_days (default) for horizons of at most k days, where every day's excess is summed.

evidence.contention_note: fan-out: up to three seats share the box; a count, contention-immune

metric_definition: peak_cost_err = |result.peak_cost - peak_price_per_kw * sum of the k largest window excesses over the threshold|, capacity_tariff golden at peak_distinct_days False, threshold 3 kW
phenomenon_property: Every top-k capacity charge, exact or surrogate, scalar or batch, sums the k largest window excesses.

null_control.value: 0.0004 with the k largest (rounding of the published figure)
null_control.note: same plans, only the top-k arm changed
